## Comparability caveats first

**All five companies are on a calendar fiscal year (Jan 1 – Dec 31), so the reporting periods themselves line up** [DOC-1].

However, **Alaska Air Group's FY2024 is not a clean like-for-like comparison** with the other four. Alaska closed its acquisition of Hawaiian Holdings on September 18, 2024, and "[t]he results of Hawaiian are included in the consolidated financial statements beginning September 18, 2024," contributing $869 million of revenue and a $113 million net loss in that stub period [DOC-2]. Alaska's FY2024 therefore blends ~8.5 months of standalone Alaska with ~3.5 months of a combined, unintegrated carrier carrying acquisition/integration drag — its ratios are depressed relative to a true organic year.

A second caveat: the excerpts provide no available seat mile (ASM) data, so true unit cost (CASM) cannot be computed [DOC-1]. What follows are **cost-to-revenue ratios**, which conflate cost discipline with pricing power/revenue premium.

## Cost ratios, FY2024

| Airline | Fuel / Rev | Labor / Rev | Fuel+Labor / Rev | Operating margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Delta | 17.1% | 26.2% | **43.4%** | **9.7%** |
| United | 20.6% | 29.2% | 49.8% | 8.9% |
| American | 21.1% | 29.6% | 50.6% | 4.8% |
| Alaska* | 21.4% | 30.6% | 51.9% | 4.9% |
| Southwest | 21.1% | 44.5% | 65.7% | 1.2% |

Underlying figures: Delta revenue $61,643M, fuel $10,566M, labor $16,161M, operating income $5,995M; United $57,063M / $11,756M / $16,678M / $5,096M; Southwest $27,483M / $5,812M / $12,240M / $321M; American $54,211M / $11,418M / $16,021M / $2,614M; Alaska $11,735M / $2,506M / $3,588M / $570M [DOC-1].

## Conclusion

**Delta** leads on every available measure: the lowest fuel burden relative to revenue (17.1% vs. 20.6–21.4% for the others), the lowest labor ratio (26.2%), the lowest combined fuel-plus-labor load (43.4%, roughly 6.5 points better than the next-best United), and the highest operating margin (9.7%) [DOC-1]. The margin gap is decisive enough that the Alaska comparability problem does not change the ranking at the top — Alaska would have to improve dramatically on a standalone basis to approach Delta.

Southwest is clearly the least efficient, with labor alone consuming 44.5% of revenue and operating margin of just 1.2% [DOC-1].

Caveat on interpretation: Delta's advantage may reflect premium-cabin and loyalty revenue (a higher denominator) as much as lower absolute costs; without ASM/CASM data this cannot be separated [DOC-1].

ANSWER: Delta Air Lines — lowest fuel/revenue (17.1%), lowest labor/revenue (26.2%), lowest combined fuel+labor/revenue (43.4%), and highest operating margin (9.7%); note Alaska's FY2024 is not fully comparable due to the mid-year Hawaiian acquisition.
